about: Each recipe is an existing, well-rated recipe from another site, credited and linked, with the ingredient list kept and the steps reworded. Scores follow research/RECIPE-RUBRIC.md: they count how much of each evidence-backed ingredient or cooking method one serving has. They are not results from trials of the dish.

categories.name: Plant polyphenols
categories.how: Fruit and vegetable servings, plus berries, cocoa, extra-virgin olive oil, herbs and spices, cooked tomato, dark greens, tea or coffee, and colour variety.

categories.name: Nrf2 & sulfur compounds
categories.how: Crucifers (raw or lightly steamed, or cooked with a myrosinase source such as mustard powder), sprouts, watercress, wasabi or horseradish, garlic and onion, turmeric.

categories.name: Fat quality
categories.how: EPA+DHA from fish, extra-virgin olive oil, nuts and seeds; points off for deep-frying, saturated-fat-heavy dishes and processed meat.

categories.name: Blood sugar & fibre
categories.how: Fibre per serving, whole-grain or legume starch, little added sugar, and carbs paired with protein or fat.

categories.name: Low-oxidant cooking
categories.how: Gentle methods (raw, steam, poach, simmer, braise) score highest; charring, well-done grilled meat, deep-frying and dark-browned starch score lowest; marinades help.

categories.name: Sperm support
categories.how: Omega-3 from fish, nuts (trials used 60–75 g/day), cooked tomato (lycopene), zinc, selenium, folate and produce; points off for processed meat, lots of sugar and alcohol.

categories.name: Egg & pregnancy support
categories.how: Folate, DHA from low-mercury fish, iron, choline, iodine, B12 and 'profertility' foods (whole grains, soy, seafood, dairy, produce); points off for high-mercury fish, alcohol and liver.

recipes.title: Strawberry Chia Overnight Oats
recipes.summary: No-cook oats soaked with milk, yogurt and chia, topped with strawberries and almonds; strong on fibre and whole grain, light on produce.

source.title: Easy Overnight Oats (6 Amazing Flavors)
source.author: Lisa Bryan
source.note: Base recipe plus the page's 'Strawberry Protein' add-in, the only add-in with berries. The original says only '1 scoop protein powder or collagen powder', with no weight or type. Scored with 2% dairy milk and plain 2% Greek yogurt. No score depends on the protein powder; kcal includes a ~25 g whey scoop (~100 kcal).

recipes.changes: Used the base recipe with the Strawberry Protein add-in, with amounts exactly as the original lists them. The protein powder and vanilla are stirred in before soaking rather than added as a topping, so the powder mixes in. Added gram and mL amounts. Steps reworded.

plants.why: Strawberries 40 g = 0.5 fruit/veg servings (+1). Berries are under 75 g, and vanilla ½ tsp is under the herb/spice amount (0). Plant families: grass (oats), mint (chia), rose (strawberry, almond) = 3; maple syrup and vanilla extract not counted (0). Total = 1 [berries-other]

nrf2.why: Base 1. No crucifers, alliums or turmeric. Total = 1

fats.why: Base 2. Chia 12 g + sliced almonds 6 g = 18 g nuts and seeds (≥15 g, +1). Saturated fat ≈3.4 g, no penalty. Total = 3 [walnuts-nuts]

glycemic.why: Fibre ≈9.6 g (oats 4.0, chia 4.1, strawberries 0.8, almonds 0.7) (+4). Whole-grain oats (+2). Maple syrup 1 tbsp ≈12 g added sugar (+1). Oats come with milk, yogurt and protein powder (+1). Total = 8 [whole-grains] [dietary-fiber-microbiome]

cooking.why: No-cook. Score 10

sperm.why: Base 1. Zinc ≈3.3 mg (oats 1.5, chia 0.55, milk 0.5, yogurt 0.3, maple 0.3, almonds 0.2) (+1). Selenium ≈27 µg (oats 11.6, chia 6.6, yogurt 5.8, milk 3.1) without counting the powder (+1). Folate ≈45 µg (0). Almonds 6 g (0). Total = 3 [zinc-status] [selenium-supplement]

egg.why: Base 1. Folate ≈45 µg, under 50 (0). Iron ≈2.9 mg (0). Choline ≈50 mg (0). Dairy is an iodine source (+1). B12 ≈1.1 µg from milk and yogurt (+1). Profertility: whole grain + dairy = 2 components (+1). Total = 4 [profertility-diet] [iodine-status] [vitamin-b12-folate-status]

items: ½ cup (120 mL) milk, dairy or dairy-free
¼ cup (60 g) Greek yogurt, dairy or dairy-free
1 scoop protein powder or collagen powder

steps: In a jar or bowl, stir together the oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds and maple syrup.
Stir in the protein powder and vanilla until no lumps remain.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight (about 8 hours), so it turns thick and creamy.
Top with the strawberries and sliced almonds just before eating.
boosts: Use ½ cup (75 g) blueberries or mixed berries instead of ¼ cup strawberries (+1 berries, +1 produce step) [blueberries]
Swap the almonds for 2 tbsp (15 g) chopped walnuts [walnuts-nuts]
Stir in 1 tbsp ground flaxseed [flaxseed-lignans]
Use 1 tsp maple syrup instead of 1 tbsp, about 4 g added sugar (+1 glycemic) [refined-sugar-high-glycemic]
Add 1 tsp cinnamon (+1 herbs and spices) [herbs-spices]
watch_outs: Pregnancy: use pasteurised milk and yogurt. Check the protein powder label for added caffeine or herbal extracts.

Allergens: dairy (milk, yogurt, whey powder), tree nuts (almonds). Oats can carry gluten unless labelled gluten-free. Collagen powder is not vegetarian; use a whey or plant protein to keep the dish vegetarian.

check.summary: Rating confirmed 4.96/310 (JSON-LD). Ingredients match the base plus Strawberry Protein add-in exactly; the original gives no weight for the powder, so no score relies on it. All seven scores confirmed; nutrients recomputed (zinc 3.3 mg, Se 27 µg without the powder); maple boost corrected so it actually changes a score.

recipes.title: Shakshuka
recipes.summary: Eggs poached in a cumin-spiced tomato and pepper sauce; strong on lycopene, produce, choline and iron.
recipes.changes: Added gram and mL amounts. Pita is kept as the original's serving suggestion but is not scored. Added a safe egg temperature for pregnancy. Steps reworded.

plants.why: Crushed tomatoes ≈198 g + bell pepper 30 g + onion 17.5 g ≈245 g = 3.1 servings (+4). Cooked tomato ≈¾ cup (+1). Fresh parsley or cilantro 1 tbsp per serving (+1). EVOO is 1½ tsp per serving, under 1 tbsp (0). Plant families: nightshade, allium, carrot family (cumin, parsley), olive = 4 (+1). Total = 7 [tomatoes-lycopene] [herbs-spices] [high-fruit-vegetable-intake]

nrf2.why: Base 1. One small onion ÷ 4 = ¼ onion per serving (+1). Garlic is 0.75 clove per serving, under 1, so no second point. Total = 2 [garlic-alliums]

fats.why: Base 2. EVOO is the main fat at 1½ tsp per serving (≥1 tsp, +1). Saturated fat ≈4.8 g, no penalty. Total = 3 [extra-virgin-olive-oil]

glycemic.why: Fibre ≈4.8 g (tomatoes 3.8, pepper 0.6, onion 0.3, herbs and spices 0.1) (+2). No starch in the dish (+2). No added sugar (+2). Vegetables come with eggs (+1). Total = 7 [glycemic-control]

cooking.why: Sauce simmered and eggs poached in it (10). Softening the onion and pepper at medium heat is the first step of a simmered dish, so no midpoint. Total = 10 [high-temperature-cooking]

sperm.why: Base 1. Cooked tomato ≥½ cup (+2). Selenium ≈26 µg, mostly from 1.5 eggs (23 µg) plus feta and tomato (+1). Zinc ≈1.9 mg (0). Folate ≈85 µg (0). Produce 3.1 servings (+1). Total = 5 [tomatoes-lycopene] [selenium-supplement] [high-fruit-vegetable-intake]

egg.why: Base 1. Folate ≈85 µg (+1). Choline ≈235 mg from 1.5 eggs (+1). Eggs and feta are iodine sources (+1). Iron ≈4.7 mg (tomatoes 2.6, eggs 1.3, spices and parsley 0.6, pepper 0.1) with ≈60 mg vitamin C from pepper and tomato (+1). B12 ≈0.85 µg (0). Profertility: dairy (feta ≈10 g) + ≥2 produce servings = 2 components (+1). Total = 6 [folic-acid] [iron-egg] [iodine-status] [profertility-diet]

items: 1 red bell pepper (about 120 g), stemmed, seeded and diced
½ tsp sea salt, plus more to taste
¼ cup fresh parsley or cilantro leaves
¼ cup (about 38 g) crumbled feta cheese

steps: Warm the olive oil in a large skillet that has a lid, over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper until soft, 5–8 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and cayenne, if using, and stir for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the tomatoes and season with the salt and pepper. Simmer on low, stirring often, until thickened, about 15 minutes.
Make six hollows in the sauce and crack an egg into each one.
Cover and cook 4–8 minutes, until the eggs are as set as you like. For pregnancy, cook until the whites and yolks are firm (160 °F / 71 °C).
Season to taste, scatter the herbs and feta over the top, and serve with pita.
boosts: Stir 2 packed cups of baby spinach or chopped kale into the sauce before adding the eggs [leafy-greens]
Use 4 garlic cloves (1 per serving); with the ¼ onion per serving that earns +2 alliums instead of +1 [garlic-alliums]
Serve with whole-wheat pita [whole-grains]
Add 2 tsp turmeric with the spices (½ tsp per serving); the oil and black pepper help absorption [turmeric-curcumin]
watch_outs: Pregnancy: cook the eggs until the whites and yolks are firm, not runny. Use feta made from pasteurised milk.
Allergens: egg, dairy (feta). Gluten if served with pita.

check.summary: Rating confirmed 4.96/189; ingredients, heat and times match. Cooking 9→10 (softening aromatics first doesn't trigger the midpoint). Egg 5→6: iron is ≈4.7 mg (canned crushed tomatoes ≈1.3 mg/100 g) with ≈60 mg vitamin C. Added 160 °F egg cue; fixed the garlic and turmeric boosts.

recipes.title: Spinach and Cheese Frittata
recipes.summary: A baked egg frittata with spinach, shallots, basil and two cheeses; very good for choline, folate and B12, but the cream and cheese push saturated fat over 10 g.
recipes.changes: Added gram and mL amounts. Added a safe egg temperature. Steps reworded.

plants.why: Spinach 35.5 g + shallots 30 g ≈65 g = 0.8 servings (+1). Raw spinach ≈1¼ packed cups per serving (+1). Fresh basil 1 tbsp per serving (+1). Plant families: amaranth (spinach), allium, mint (basil), olive = 4 (+1). Total = 4 [leafy-greens] [herbs-spices]

nrf2.why: Base 1. Shallots ≈30 g per serving, more than ¼ of a medium onion (≈27 g) (+1). Total = 2 [garlic-alliums]

fats.why: Base 2. EVOO 1½ tsp per serving as the cooking fat (+1). Saturated fat ≈14.8 g (cream 4.6, Cheddar 4.0, eggs 3.1, Parmesan 2.1, oil 1.0), over 10 g (−2). Total = 1 [extra-virgin-olive-oil]

glycemic.why: Fibre ≈1.8 g (+1). No starch (+2). No added sugar (+2). The little carbohydrate comes with eggs (+1). Total = 6

cooking.why: Baked at 325 °F / 165 °C (10). Softening the shallots and wilting the spinach is the first step of a baked dish, so no midpoint. Total = 10 [high-temperature-cooking]

sperm.why: Base 1. Selenium ≈40 µg (eggs 31, cheeses 9) (+1). Folate ≈134 µg (+1). Zinc ≈2.8 mg, under 3 (0). Produce 0.8 servings (0). Total = 3 [selenium-supplement]

egg.why: Base 1. Folate ≈134 µg (spinach 69, eggs 44, shallots 10, cheese 7) (+2). Choline ≈313 mg from 2 eggs (+1). Eggs and dairy are iodine sources (+1). B12 ≈1.3 µg (+1). Iron ≈3.2 mg (0). Profertility: dairy only, produce 0.8 servings (0). Total = 6 [folic-acid] [iodine-status] [vitamin-b12-folate-status]

items: ¾ cup (about 120 g) thinly sliced shallots, from 2–3 shallots
5 oz (142 g) baby spinach, about 5 packed cups
¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
¾ cup (about 85 g) shredded Cheddar cheese
½ cup (about 50 g) grated Parmigiano Reggiano

steps: Heat the oven to 325 °F (165 °C) with a rack in the middle.
Warm the oil in a 10-inch ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Cook the shallots 3–4 minutes until soft but not browned.
Add half the spinach and let it wilt, about 1 minute. Add the rest with ¼ tsp salt and cook 1–2 minutes more.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, cream, pepper and the remaining ¼ tsp salt. Stir in the spinach mixture, both cheeses and the basil.
Pour everything back into the skillet and bake 20–23 minutes, until the centre is set and no longer wet (160 °F / 71 °C).
Use an oven mitt, because the handle will be hot. Serve from the pan or slide the frittata onto a plate.
boosts: Use milk instead of heavy cream and halve the Cheddar to bring saturated fat under 10 g per serving (+2 fats) [mediterranean-diet]
Double the spinach to 10 oz (284 g) [leafy-greens]
Fold in 1 cup halved cherry tomatoes [tomatoes-lycopene]
Serve with whole-grain toast [whole-grains]
watch_outs: Pregnancy: bake until fully set. Parmigiano Reggiano is made from raw milk, but hard aged cheeses are generally considered low-risk. Check with your provider if unsure.
Allergens: egg, dairy.
Parmigiano Reggiano is made with animal rennet; strict vegetarians can use a Parmesan-style cheese made with microbial rennet.

check.summary: Rating confirmed 4.92/102 (reviews, not the 163 comments); ingredients, 325 °F and 20–23 min match. Cooking 9→10 (sautéing shallots and spinach first doesn't trigger the midpoint). Other scores confirmed; nutrients refined. Added 160 °F cue and a rennet note.

recipes.title: Classic Hummus
recipes.summary: Whipped chickpea, tahini, lemon and olive-oil dip; a fibre-rich legume snack, but a ¼-cup portion of canned-chickpea hummus is too small to score on fertility nutrients.

source.title: Easy Hummus (Better than Store-Bought)
source.author: Joanne Gallagher
source.note: Rating and count read from the recipe card (1,980 reviews; the 3,204 comments are separate). Scored with canned chickpeas, the original's first option.

recipes.changes: Dropped the paprika, sumac or za'atar garnish. Steps reworded.

plants.why: Chickpeas ≈42 g per ¼-cup serving = 0.5 servings; legumes count as at most one serving (+1). EVOO is 1 tsp per serving and cumin a trace, so no item points. Plant families: legume, sesame, olive, citrus, allium, carrot family (cumin) = 6 (+1). Total = 2 [legumes]

nrf2.why: Base 1. One small clove split 6 ways is too little garlic (0). Total = 1

fats.why: Base 2. EVOO 2 tbsp ÷ 6 = 1 tsp per serving (+1). Tahini is 10 g per serving, under 15 g (0). Total = 3 [extra-virgin-olive-oil]

glycemic.why: Fibre ≈4.1 g (chickpeas 3.2, tahini 0.9) (+2). The starch is a legume (+2). No added sugar (+2). Comes with tahini and EVOO fat (+1). Total = 7 [legumes] [dietary-fiber-microbiome]

cooking.why: No-cook. Score 10

sperm.why: Base 1. Folate ≈40 µg, zinc ≈0.9 mg and selenium ≈5 µg all fall below the thresholds. Total = 1

egg.why: Base 1. Folate ≈40 µg: canned chickpeas ≈105 µg per cup, so 42 g ≈27 µg, plus tahini ≈10 µg and lemon ≈2 µg; under 50 (0). Iron ≈1.5 mg (0). Total = 1

items: 1 (15-oz) can chickpeas, drained, or 1½ cups (250 g) cooked chickpeas
¼ cup (60 mL) fresh lemon juice, from about 1 large lemon
2 tbsp (30 mL) extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
½ tsp salt, or to taste
2–3 tbsp (30–45 mL) cold water or aquafaba

steps: Blend the tahini and lemon juice in a food processor for 1 minute. Scrape down the bowl and blend 30 seconds more, until pale and whipped.
Add the olive oil, garlic, cumin and salt and blend until combined.
Add the chickpeas in two additions, processing after each until thick and fairly smooth.
With the motor running, pour in 2–3 tbsp cold water or aquafaba until the hummus is silky.
Taste and adjust the salt and lemon, then serve drizzled with a little olive oil.
boosts: Serve with raw broccoli florets, radishes or cauliflower as dippers; 80 g of raw crucifers earns +5 Nrf2 [cruciferous-other]
Dust with ½ tsp sumac or smoked paprika [herbs-spices]
Serve with red-pepper and carrot sticks instead of pita [high-fruit-vegetable-intake]
Use home-cooked chickpeas, which keep more folate than canned (≈280 vs ≈105 µg per cup), lifting folate to ≈85 µg (+1 egg) [legumes]
watch_outs: Allergens: sesame (tahini).

check.summary: Rating confirmed 4.9/1,980; ingredients and method match. Egg 2→1: the recipe specifies canned chickpeas, so folate is ≈40 µg, not 80. Chickpea boost now gives its effect.

recipes.title: Sautéed Kale with Red Wine Vinegar
recipes.summary: A big pile of kale steamed in stock with garlic and olive oil, then finished with red wine vinegar; over two produce servings and plenty of fibre and folate, but cooking leaves little myrosinase.

source.title: Sauteed Kale
source.author: Bobby Flay
source.note: Replaces Love and Lemons 'Sautéed Kale' (4.98 from 40 votes). The rating only loads with JavaScript, so it was read from the page's JSON-LD (ratingValue 4.5, reviewCount 307) in a browser.

recipes.changes: Replaced the finder's under-100-rating recipe with this one. Added gram and mL amounts. Split the single method paragraph into steps and added an approximate time for cooking off the liquid. Steps reworded.

The oil is plain olive oil, not extra-virgin, and there are no herbs or spices beyond pepper (0). Plant families: crucifer, allium, olive = 3 (0). Total = 4 [leafy-greens] [high-fruit-vegetable-intake]

nrf2.why: Base 1. Kale 170 g per serving, cooked covered in stock 5 min and then until the liquid evaporates, so the cooked tier, with no raw myrosinase source (+3). Garlic is ½ clove per serving (0). Total = 4 [cruciferous-other]

fats.why: Base 2. The recipe calls for olive oil, not extra-virgin, so no EVOO points (0). No nuts or seeds, no penalties. Total = 2 [cooking-oil-choice]

glycemic.why: Fibre ≈7.0 g from 170 g kale (+3). No starch (+2). No added sugar (+2). Comes with olive oil (≈2¼ tsp per serving) and red wine vinegar (+1). Total = 8 [dietary-fiber-microbiome]

cooking.why: The kale is steamed and braised in stock under a lid, and the uncovered finish only cooks off the liquid, without browning (10). Softening the garlic first doesn't lower the score. Total = 10 [high-temperature-cooking]

sperm.why: Base 1. Folate ≈105 µg (kale ≈62 µg per 100 g raw) (+1). Produce 2.1 servings (+1). Zinc ≈0.7 mg and selenium ≈1.5 µg (0). Total = 3 [high-fruit-vegetable-intake]

egg.why: Base 1. Folate ≈105 µg (+2). Iron ≈2.7 mg, under 4 (0). No iodine source, choline or B12 (0). Profertility: ≥2 produce servings is only one component (0). Total = 3 [folic-acid]

items: 1½ lb (680 g) young kale, stems and leaves coarsely chopped
½ cup (120 mL) vegetable stock or water

steps: Warm the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and cook just until soft, without letting it colour.
Turn the heat up to high, add the stock or water and the kale, and toss together.
Put the lid on and cook for 5 minutes.
Take off the lid and keep stirring until the liquid has cooked away, a few minutes more.
Season with salt and pepper, then stir in the vinegar.
boosts: Use extra-virgin olive oil; at about 2¼ tsp per serving it earns +1 fats [extra-virgin-olive-oil]
After cooking, toss in ½ tsp mustard powder or a handful of raw rocket so the cooked kale gets a raw myrosinase source (+5 instead of +3 Nrf2) [mustard-seed-myrosinase]
Use 4 garlic cloves (1 per serving) [garlic-alliums]
Top each serving with 2 tbsp (15 g) toasted chopped walnuts [walnuts-nuts]

source.note: Test-kitchen recipe (ATK). Rated 4.34 by 40 members, below the 4.5 / 100-rating target. No mussels-in-tomato recipe with ≥100 ratings could be verified on sites that allow fetching. The recipe sits behind ATK's member paywall.

recipes.changes: Serves 4–6 in the original; scored at 4 main-course servings. Gram and mL conversions added; steps reworded.

plants.why: Crushed tomatoes 794 g ÷ 4 ≈ 200 g/serving = 2.5 servings (+3) [high-fruit-vegetable-intake]; cooked tomato product ≥½ cup (+1) [tomatoes-lycopene]; EVOO only ¾ tsp/serving and parsley ½ tbsp/serving, both below thresholds (0); ≥4 plant families: nightshades, alliums, olive, parsley, grape (+1) = 5

nrf2.why: Base 1; garlic 3 cloves ÷ 4 = 0.75 clove/serving, under the 1-clove threshold (0); no crucifers. = 1

fats.why: Base 2; ≈110 g cooked mussel meat/serving (≈25% yield from 4 lb in shell) × ~0.8 g/100 g ≈ 860 mg EPA+DHA (+4) [omega3-fish]; EVOO 1 tbsp ÷ 4 is under 1 tsp/serving (0). 2 + 4 = 6

glycemic.why: Fibre ≈4 g from tomatoes (+2); no starch in the recipe, since bread is only a serving suggestion (+2); no added sugar (+2); tomato carbohydrate comes with mussel protein (+1) = 7

cooking.why: Mussels steamed in simmering sauce under foil; tomato paste cooked only until slightly darkened. Steam/simmer = 10

sperm.why: Base 1; EPA+DHA ≥500 mg (+3) [omega3-fish]; cooked tomato ≥½ cup (+2) [tomatoes-lycopene]; zinc ≈3.3 mg (+1) [zinc-status]; selenium ≈100 µg (+1); folate ≈112 µg (+1); produce 2.5 servings (+1). Wine simmers ≈21–24 min in total (1 min boil + 5 min reduce + 15–18 min covered in the oven), so ≥15 min and no penalty [alcohol]. 1 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 10

egg.why: Base 1; folate ≈112 µg (+2); EPA+DHA ≥500 mg from low-mercury mussels (+2) [omega3-fish]; iron ≈10 mg, with ≈34 mg vitamin C covering the tomato's plant iron (+1) [iron-egg]; choline ≈100 mg (0); seafood iodine (+1); B12 ≈26 µg (+1); seafood + ≥2 produce servings = 2 different profertility components (+1). 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 9

items: 4 lb (1.8 kg) mussels, scrubbed and debearded

steps: Throw out any mussels that smell bad, have cracked shells or won't close when tapped. Set a rack in the lowest position and heat the oven to 500 °F (260 °C).
In a large roasting pan over medium heat, stir the oil, tomato paste, garlic and pepper flakes for about 2 minutes, until fragrant and the paste has darkened a little.
Pour in the wine, bring it to the boil and let it reduce for about 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and salt, turn the heat to high and cook, stirring often, for about 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in the mussels, cover the pan tightly with foil and bake 15–18 minutes, until most shells have opened.
Discard any mussels that stayed closed, toss with the parsley and serve.
boosts: Use 4–6 garlic cloves (≥1 per serving) [garlic-alliums]
Finish each bowl with 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil [extra-virgin-olive-oil]
Scatter a generous handful of parsley or basil (≥1 tbsp per serving) [herbs-spices]
Serve with whole-grain bread to soak up the sauce [whole-grains]
watch_outs: Pregnancy: the sauce holds ¼ cup wine per serving. It cooks for about 20 minutes, which removes most but not all of the alcohol. Use low-sodium broth or clam juice instead for a fully alcohol-free version.
Pregnancy: eat only mussels that have opened fully during cooking, and discard any that stay closed.
Mercury: mussels are very low in mercury.
Allergens: shellfish (molluscs)

recipes.title: Cioppino (San Francisco fish stew)
recipes.summary: A wine-and-tomato seafood stew with baked fish, clams and shrimp. Omega-3, EVOO, lycopene, selenium and choline score high; the butter and long prep keep it from being a weeknight dish.
recipes.changes: Serves 4–6 in the original; scored at 4 servings (the site's nutrition panel uses 4). Parsley garnish dropped. Gram and mL conversions added; steps reworded. EPA+DHA assumes cod as the fish.

plants.why: Crushed tomatoes ≈200 g + shallots ≈27 g/serving ≈ 2.8 servings (+3) [high-fruit-vegetable-intake]; EVOO 6 tbsp ÷ 4 = 1.5 tbsp/serving (+1) [extra-virgin-olive-oil]; cooked tomato ≥½ cup (+1) [tomatoes-lycopene]; thyme, oregano and chili together are under 1 tsp dried per serving (0); ≥4 plant families: nightshades, alliums, olive, mint, grape (+1) = 6

nrf2.why: Base 1; shallots ⅔ cup ÷ 4 ≈ 27 g/serving ≈ ¼ onion (+1) [garlic-alliums]; garlic 0.75 clove/serving doesn't add a second allium point; no crucifers. 1 + 1 = 2

fats.why: Base 2; per serving ≈145 g cooked cod (≈290 mg) + ≈140 g shrimp (≈420 mg) + clams (≈60 mg) ≈ 770 mg EPA+DHA (+4) [omega3-fish]; EVOO is the main fat at 1.5 tbsp/serving (+2), with butter only ¾ tbsp; sat fat ≈8 g, no penalty. 2 + 4 + 2 = 8

glycemic.why: Fibre ≈4.8 g (+2); no starch in the recipe, since bread is a serving suggestion (+2); sugar 2 tsp ÷ 4 ≈ 2 g/serving (+2); tomato carbohydrate comes with seafood protein (+1) = 7

cooking.why: Stew simmered (10); the fish is baked separately at 400 °F (205 °C) (8), a separate harsher component, so the midpoint applies = 9

sperm.why: Base 1; EPA+DHA ≥500 mg (+3) [omega3-fish]; cooked tomato ≥½ cup (+2) [tomatoes-lycopene]; zinc ≈4.1 mg (+1) [zinc-status]; selenium ≈150 µg (+1); folate ≈73 µg (0); produce 2.8 servings (+1). Wine boils 3–4 min, then simmers 25 min covered plus ≈11 min with the shellfish, so ≥15 min and no penalty [alcohol]. 1 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 9

egg.why: Base 1; folate ≈73 µg (+1); EPA+DHA ≥500 mg from low-mercury cod, shrimp and clams (+2) [omega3-fish]; iron ≈4.4 mg is mostly plant iron with only ≈22 mg vitamin C (0); choline ≈340 mg from shrimp and fish (+1); seafood iodine (+1); B12 ≈16 µg (+1); seafood + ≥2 produce servings = 2 different components (+1). 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 8

items: ¼ cup + 2 tbsp (90 mL) extra-virgin olive oil, divided
⅔ cup (about 100 g) finely chopped shallots (about 3)
2 bottles (8 oz / 240 mL each) clam juice
½ tsp crushed red pepper flakes
7 sprigs fresh thyme, plus 1 tsp chopped thyme
1½ lb (680 g) firm fish fillets (halibut, cod, salmon or snapper), cut into 2-in (5 cm) pieces
1½ lb (680 g; about 18) littleneck clams, scrubbed
1½ lb (680 g) extra-large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined

steps: Heat the oven to 400 °F (205 °C) with a rack in the middle, and line a baking sheet with foil.
Warm ¼ cup of the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the shallots about 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute without letting it brown.
Pour in the wine, turn the heat to high and boil 3–4 minutes until it has reduced by about half.
Add the tomatoes, clam juice, sugar, 1 tsp salt, pepper flakes, oregano, thyme sprigs and the water. Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer gently for 25 minutes.
While it simmers, toss the fish with the remaining 2 tbsp oil and ¾ tsp salt, spread it on the sheet and bake about 10 minutes until just cooked through (145 °F / 63 °C). Keep it covered and warm.

Remove the thyme sprigs, stir in the butter and add the clams. Return to a simmer, cover and cook about 6 minutes until most clams open. Add the shrimp and simmer, covered, about 5 minutes more until the shrimp are opaque and all the clams are open; discard any that stay shut. Stir in the chopped thyme and adjust the seasoning.
Divide the fish among bowls and ladle the stew, clams and shrimp over the top.
boosts: Use salmon as the fish to push EPA+DHA well above 1,500 mg per serving [omega3-fish]
Use 4 or more garlic cloves (≥1 per serving) [garlic-alliums]
Replace the butter with extra-virgin olive oil [extra-virgin-olive-oil]
Serve with whole-grain bread rather than white baguette [whole-grains]
watch_outs: Pregnancy: the stew contains ¼ cup wine per serving. It simmers well over 15 minutes, so most of the alcohol cooks off, but not all; replace it with extra clam juice or broth for a fully alcohol-free version.
Pregnancy: cook until the clams are fully open, the shrimp are opaque and the fish reaches 145 °F (63 °C).
Mercury: choose cod, salmon or snapper. Halibut is an FDA 'good choice', so eat it less often. Never substitute swordfish, king mackerel or other high-mercury fish.
Allergens: fish, shellfish (crustaceans and molluscs), dairy (butter)

recipes.title: Salt-baked mackerel (saba shioyaki)
recipes.summary: Japanese-style mackerel salted, then baked until golden and served with grated raw daikon. It's one of the richest omega-3 dishes in the set, but too little plant food to score on polyphenols.

source.title: Grilled Mackerel (Saba Shioyaki)
source.author: Namiko Chen
source.note: Despite the name, the recipe bakes the fish in the oven.

recipes.changes: Gram conversions added; storage notes dropped; steps reworded. EPA+DHA uses Atlantic mackerel values; Pacific chub mackerel would be higher.

plants.why: Grated daikon 75 g ÷ 2, squeezed ≈ under 0.5 serving (0); no high-polyphenol items (0); only 3 plant families: radish, citrus, soy (0). Total 0, floored at 1

nrf2.why: Base 1; raw daikon ≈37 g/serving is under the 40 g crucifer threshold (0); daikon isn't a listed concentrated isothiocyanate source (0). = 1

fats.why: Base 2; 140 g raw fillet ≈ 110 g cooked × ~1.2 g/100 g (Atlantic mackerel) ≈ 1,300 mg EPA+DHA (+5) [omega3-fish]; no added fat; sat fat ≈4.6 g. 2 + 5 = 7

glycemic.why: Fibre ≈0.7 g (0); no starch (+2); no added sugar (+2); the trace carbohydrate comes with fish protein (+1) = 5

cooking.why: Fish baked at 425 °F (218 °C), in the 200–220 °C fish band = 8 [high-temperature-cooking]

sperm.why: Base 1; EPA+DHA ≥500 mg (+3) [omega3-fish]; selenium ≈57 µg (+1) [selenium-supplement]; zinc ≈1 mg (0); folate ≈12 µg (0); produce under 2 servings (0). 1 + 3 + 1 = 5

egg.why: Base 1; folate ≈12 µg (0); EPA+DHA ≥500 mg from low-mercury Atlantic or chub mackerel (+2) [omega3-fish] [mercury-fish]; iron ≈1.7 mg (0); choline ≈80 mg (0); seafood iodine (+1); B12 ≈21 µg (+1) [vitamin-b12-folate-status]; only one profertility component, seafood (0). 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 5

items: ½ tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt
1-inch piece daikon radish (2.6 oz / 75 g), for grating

steps: Rub the fillets with the sake, then pat them dry (discard the sake) and set them on a baking sheet lined with parchment.
Sprinkle both sides with the salt and leave at room temperature for 20 minutes. Meanwhile heat the oven to 425 °F (218 °C), or 25 °F (15 °C) lower with convection.
Blot off the moisture the salt has drawn out.
Bake skin-side down for 15–20 minutes, until the top is golden and the flesh flakes easily (145 °F / 63 °C).
Peel and finely grate the daikon and squeeze out most of its liquid. Serve the fish with the daikon and lemon, with a few drops of soy sauce on the daikon.
boosts: Serve 80 g or more of grated raw daikon per person to earn the raw-crucifer +5 [cruciferous-other]
Add a side of watercress salad (≥½ cup raw) [watercress-peitc]
Serve with brown rice and a cooked leafy-green side [whole-grains] [leafy-greens]
watch_outs: Mercury: use Atlantic or Pacific chub (saba) mackerel, which are low-mercury FDA 'best choices'. Never use king mackerel (high mercury). Spanish mackerel is a 'good choice', so eat it less often.
Pregnancy: bake until the flesh flakes (145 °F / 63 °C).
Alcohol: the sake is rubbed on and discarded before baking, so almost none remains; you can skip it.
Allergens: fish, soy and gluten (soy sauce; use tamari for gluten-free)

recipes.title: Avgolemono (Greek lemon chicken soup)
recipes.summary: Chicken and rice soup thickened with a blended egg-lemon mixture; it's gentle to cook and gives good choline, but has almost no vegetables, and its optional cream adds saturated fat.
recipes.changes: Serves 4–6 in the original; scored at 4 servings. The optional cream is included as written. Gram and mL conversions added; steps reworded.

plants.why: Lemon juice ≈19 g/serving ≈ 0.2 servings (0); dill ½ tsp fresh/serving is below threshold (0); ≥4 plant families: rice, citrus, dill, bay, pepper (+1) = 1

nrf2.why: Base 1; no crucifers, alliums or turmeric. = 1

fats.why: Base 2; no omega-3, EVOO or nuts; heavy cream (½ cup ÷ 4 = 2 tbsp, ≈11 g fat/serving) is the main fat (−2); sat fat ≈9 g. 2 − 2 = 0, floored at 1

glycemic.why: Fibre ≈0.5 g (0); white rice is a refined starch (0) [whole-grains]; no added sugar (+2); rice comes with chicken and egg (+1) = 3

cooking.why: Chicken gently poached in hot broth; soup simmered. Poach/simmer = 10

sperm.why: Base 1; selenium ≈43 µg (+1); natural food folate ≈36 µg, ignoring rice fortification (0); zinc ≈1.9 mg (0); produce under 2 servings (0). 1 + 1 = 2

egg.why: Base 1; natural food folate ≈36 µg from eggs, lemon and chicken, ignoring folic acid in enriched rice (0); no omega-3 (0); iron ≈2.4 mg (0); choline ≈225 mg from eggs, yolks and chicken (+1); egg and dairy iodine (+1) [iodine-status]; B12 ≈0.8 µg (0); only one profertility component, dairy (0). 1 + 1 + 1 = 3

items: 1 lb (450 g) chicken tenderloins (or breasts cut into 1-in / 2.5 cm strips)
¾ cup (140 g) long-grain white rice
3 sprigs fresh dill, plus 2 tsp chopped dill
5 tbsp (75 mL) fresh lemon juice (from 2 lemons)
½ cup (120 mL) heavy cream, plus a little more if needed (optional)
Freshly ground black pepper, for serving

steps: Salt the chicken all over and let it stand for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile bring the broth, rice, white pepper, dill sprigs and bay leaf to the boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook about 5 minutes until the rice is al dente.
Take the pot off the heat, add the chicken, cover and leave about 15 minutes until it's cooked through (165 °F / 74 °C). Discard the dill sprigs and bay leaf, then lift out the chicken and chop it.

Spoon about ¾ cup of the rice into a blender with the lemon juice, eggs and yolks and blend until smooth. With the lid vented, blend in a ladle (about ¾ cup / 180 mL) of hot broth, then a second ladle.
Pour the egg mixture slowly into the pot while stirring, add the cream, and bring to a gentle simmer over low heat without boiling. Simmer a little longer if the rice still needs it.
Stir in the chopped dill and chicken and adjust the seasoning: add more cream if it's too tart, or water if it's too thick. Serve right away, as it thickens on standing.
boosts: Leave out the optional cream to remove the −2 fat penalty [mediterranean-diet]
Stir 2 cups of chopped spinach into the pot in the last minute [leafy-greens]
Simmer a diced carrot, onion and celery stalk in the broth first [high-fruit-vegetable-intake] [garlic-alliums]
Use brown rice (cook it longer before adding the chicken) [whole-grains]
watch_outs: Pregnancy: the eggs are only cooked by the soup's heat. Make sure the soup returns to a gentle simmer (at least 160 °F / 71 °C) after the egg mixture goes in, and cook the chicken to 165 °F (74 °C).
Check the broth label if you need it gluten-free.
Allergens: egg, dairy (cream)

recipes.title: Tandoori chicken (yogurt-marinated)
recipes.summary: Skinless chicken marinated overnight in spiced yogurt and lemon, then roasted hot and briefly broiled. The marinade softens the high-heat penalty, but on its own the dish brings little produce or omega-3.
recipes.changes: Gram and mL conversions added; coriander garnish and air-fryer variation dropped; serving suggestions condensed; steps reworded.

plants.why: No fruit or veg in the recipe (0); garam masala, chili, coriander, cumin, pepper, turmeric and methi ≈6 tsp ÷ 4 ≈ 1.5 tsp dried/serving (+1) [herbs-spices]; ≥4 plant families: cumin/coriander, chili, ginger/turmeric, garlic, fenugreek, citrus (+1) = 2

nrf2.why: Base 1; ginger-garlic paste ≈0.4 clove/serving (0); turmeric ¼ tsp ÷ 4 is far below ½ tsp/serving (0). = 1

fats.why: Base 2; no omega-3 (≈20 mg); neutral oil, not EVOO (0); skinless chicken, sat fat ≈6 g, no penalty. = 2

glycemic.why: Fibre ≈0.6 g (0); no starch (+2); no added sugar (+2); trace carbohydrate comes with protein (+1) = 5

cooking.why: Poultry roasted at 470 °F (240 °C) then broiled 3–4 min to charred spots, cooked to well done = 4, raised to 6 by the ≥6-hour yogurt-lemon-spice marinade [marinating-meat] [high-temperature-cooking]. Heavier charring would drop it to 2

sperm.why: Base 1; ≈100 g cooked dark meat gives zinc ≈2.9 mg, just under 3 (0); selenium ≈28 µg (+1); folate ≈15 µg (0); no produce (0). 1 + 1 = 2

egg.why: Base 1; folate, omega-3 and iron all below thresholds (0); choline ≈85 mg (0); yogurt (dairy) iodine (+1) [iodine-status]; B12 ≈0.6 µg (0); only one profertility component, dairy (0). 1 + 1 = 2

items: ¾ kg (1½ lb) skinless bone-in chicken thighs or legs (or 8 drumsticks; 4 portions)
½ cup (about 120 g) Greek yogurt (hung curd)
1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (or ¾ tbsp each grated ginger and garlic)
1–2 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder (or paprika)
1½ tbsp (22 mL) neutral oil or mustard oil
1 tbsp (15 mL) lemon juice (or 1 tsp amchur, or ½ tsp chaat masala)
1–2 tbsp (15–30 mL) neutral oil or mustard oil

steps: Stir the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, spices, salt, methi, oil and lemon juice into a marinade, then taste and adjust the salt and heat.
Cut 3–4 deep slashes in each leg or thigh (2–3 in drumsticks), coat thoroughly, cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours, and up to 36.
Take the chicken out 20 minutes before cooking. Heat the oven to 470 °F (240 °C), or 430 °F (220 °C) in a small countertop oven, and set an oiled wire rack over a foil-lined tray.
Space the pieces on the rack and roast 15 minutes, then baste with leftover marinade or with the basting chili powder stirred into the oil.
For thighs or legs, turn them and roast another 12–15 minutes, basting again (drumsticks and breasts skip this).
Broil on the top rack 3–4 minutes until a few spots char and the thickest part reads 165 °F (74 °C). Optionally brush with melted butter and dust with chaat masala before serving.
boosts: Skip or shorten the final broil to limit charring [high-temperature-cooking]
Serve with the author's suggested kachumber (cucumber, tomato, onion salad), about 1 cup per person [high-fruit-vegetable-intake]
Raise the turmeric to ½ tsp per serving; the marinade already has oil and black pepper [turmeric-curcumin]
Choose avocado or mustard oil rather than grapeseed for the high-heat roast [cooking-oil-choice]
watch_outs: Pregnancy: cook to 165 °F (74 °C) at the bone.
High heat: broiling to char forms heterocyclic amines, so keep charred spots small.
Allergens: dairy (yogurt; optional butter)

recipes.title: Beef and broccoli stir-fry
recipes.summary: A takeaway-style stir-fry of quickly seared beef and blanched broccoli in a glossy soy sauce. Plenty of broccoli gives solid Nrf2 points; a spoonful of rice wine costs it fertility points.
recipes.changes: Serves 3–4 in the original; scored at 3 servings. Sesame-seed garnish dropped. Gram and mL conversions added; the broccoli par-boil from the recipe notes is included as a step; steps reworded.

plants.why: Broccoli ≈120 g/serving = 1.5 servings (+2); ginger, five-spice and pepper together are far below 1 tsp dried per serving (0); ≥4 plant families: crucifer, allium, ginger, soy, sesame, rice wine (+1) = 3

nrf2.why: Base 1; broccoli ≈120 g/serving (≥80 g), par-boiled 40 s–1 min and then simmered in the sauce: boiled or simmered counts as cooked, however short (+3) [broccoli-mature]; garlic 1 clove ÷ 3 servings (0). 1 + 3 = 4

fats.why: Base 2; no omega-3, EVOO or nuts; lean beef, no processed meat; sat fat ≈3.8 g. = 2

glycemic.why: Fibre ≈3.5 g (+2; panel says 4.1 g); no starch in the recipe, since the suggested rice isn't part of it (+2); sugar 1 tsp ÷ 3 plus dark soy ≈ 2 g (+2); carbohydrate comes with beef (+1) = 7

cooking.why: Thin-sliced beef and broccoli stir-fried in oil and finished in a simmering sauce; the beef is browned for about 1 minute and only just cooked through, not well done. Stir-fry row = 8; no separate harsher component, so no midpoint. Oil type isn't specified; a PUFA seed oil would not change this, as there's no long high-heat frying [high-temperature-cooking]

sperm.why: Base 1; ≈90 g cooked beef gives zinc ≈5 mg (+1, ≥3 but under 5.5) [zinc-status]; selenium ≈29 µg (+1); folate ≈75 µg (0); produce 1.5 servings (0); 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine simmers only about 1 min (−1) [alcohol]. 1 + 1 + 1 − 1 = 2

egg.why: Base 1; folate ≈75 µg (+1); iron ≈3 mg (0); choline ≈100 mg (0); no named iodine source (0); B12 ≈2.2 µg (+1); no profertility components (0); Shaoxing wine not cooked off (−2) [alcohol]. 1 + 1 + 1 − 2 = 1

items: 12 oz (360 g) beef fillet, flank or rump
4–5 cups broccoli florets (1 head, about 300–350 g), par-boiled

steps: Par-boil the broccoli: drop it into boiling water and, once the water returns to the boil, cook 40 seconds (just done) to 1 minute (tender), then drain.
Stir the cornstarch into the ¼ cup water, then mix in the rest of the sauce ingredients.
Slice the beef ¼ in (5 mm) thick and toss it with 2 tbsp of the sauce.

Heat the oil in a skillet over high heat, spread the beef out and leave it 1 minute to brown. Stir for 10 seconds, add the garlic and ginger, and stir 30 seconds more until the beef is no longer pink.
Pour in the remaining sauce and the 1 cup water and stir. When it bubbles, add the broccoli and simmer about 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Take it off the heat immediately and serve; the original suggests rice.
boosts: Replace the Shaoxing wine with low-sodium chicken broth, as the recipe's own note allows (+1 sperm, +2 egg) [alcohol]
Marinate the sliced beef in the sauce and ginger for 30 minutes first [marinating-meat]
Use 3 garlic cloves (1 per serving) [garlic-alliums]
Serve over brown rice [whole-grains]
watch_outs: Pregnancy: the 1 tbsp of Shaoxing wine is barely cooked. The amount per serving is tiny, but swap in broth to avoid it entirely. Cook the beef until no pink remains.
Allergens: soy, gluten (soy sauce and Shaoxing wine contain wheat), sesame (optional sesame oil)

recipes.title: Moroccan chicken with chickpeas and couscous
recipes.summary: A one-pot oven braise of spiced chicken breasts with chickpeas, fire-roasted tomatoes, kale, raisins and pearl couscous. Gentle braising, spices and fibre score well, but small servings and refined couscous hold the rest back.

source.title: Moroccan Chicken Couscous
source.author: Joanna Cismaru
source.note: Chosen as the chicken-and-chickpea braise. Once Upon a Chef's Moroccan Chicken Tagine (4.8 / 240) has no chickpeas, and RecipeTin Eats' Chicken Tagine with chickpeas has only 66 ratings.

recipes.changes: Gram and mL conversions added; the kale (≈100 g) and couscous (≈170 g) weights are estimates. Steps reworded, with a 165 °F (74 °C) doneness cue added.

plants.why: Per serving: tomatoes ≈50 g + onion ≈19 g + kale ≈12 g + garlic ≈2 g ≈ 1.0 serving, plus raisins 10 g ≈ 0.33 and chickpeas 30 g ≈ 0.4 (legumes capped at 1 serving) ≈ 1.8 servings (+2); spice blend without salt ≈7.75 tsp ÷ 8 ≈ 1 tsp dried/serving (+1, borderline) [herbs-spices]; tomato (≈¼ cup) and kale (½ cup raw) are both under threshold (0); ≥4 plant families: wheat, legume, crucifer, nightshade, allium, grape, cumin/coriander, cinnamon, ginger (+1) = 4

nrf2.why: Base 1; kale ≈12 g/serving is under 40 g (0); garlic 5 cloves ÷ 8 ≈ 0.6 clove and onion ⅛/serving are both below threshold (0); turmeric ½ tsp ÷ 8 is under ½ tsp/serving (0). = 1

fats.why: Base 2; no omega-3; 'olive oil' (not specified as EVOO) at ¾ tsp/serving (0); lean chicken breast, sat fat ≈1.2 g. = 2

glycemic.why: Fibre ≈5.5 g from chickpeas, couscous, raisins and veg (+3; the recipe panel claims 8 g) [legumes]; the main starch is refined pearl couscous, with chickpeas the smaller share (0) [whole-grains]; raisins are fruit, so no added sugar (+2); couscous comes with chicken and chickpeas (+1) = 6

cooking.why: Oven-braised, covered then uncovered, at 375 °F = 10. The brief initial sear is the first step of the braise, not a separate component, so there's no midpoint

sperm.why: Base 1; tomato ≈50 g/serving is under ½ cup (0); zinc ≈1.5 mg (0); selenium ≈34 µg (+1); folate ≈46 µg (0); produce 1.8 servings (0). 1 + 1 = 2

egg.why: Base 1; natural food folate ≈46 µg: canned chickpeas ≈19 µg (≈105 µg per cup) plus kale and tomato (0); iron ≈3.1 mg (0); choline ≈74 mg (0); no named iodine source (0); B12 ≈0.2 µg (0); no profertility components (0). = 1

items: 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 1½ lb / 680 g)
1 can (14 oz / 400 g) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
4 cups (about 100 g) kale, rinsed and roughly chopped

steps: Heat the oven to 375 °F (190 °C) and mix the spice blend.
Rub the chicken breasts all over with 2 tbsp of the blend.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven or other ovenproof pot over medium-high heat and sear the chicken 2–3 minutes per side, until browned outside but not cooked through. Set it aside.
Cook the onion and garlic in the pot for about 3 minutes until soft and fragrant, then stir in the last 1 tbsp of the blend.
Add the raisins, chickpeas, tomatoes, broth and couscous, stir well and fold in the kale. Bring to the boil and nestle the chicken back in.
Cover with a lid or foil and bake 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 30 minutes more, until the couscous is tender and the chicken reaches 165 °F (74 °C).
boosts: Double the kale (8 cups) [leafy-greens]
Add a second can of chickpeas [legumes]
Use a 28-oz (794 g) can of tomatoes for ≥½ cup cooked tomato per serving [tomatoes-lycopene]
Sear in extra-virgin olive oil and drizzle 1 tsp more per serving at the table [extra-virgin-olive-oil]
Use whole-wheat pearl couscous if you can find it [whole-grains]
watch_outs: Pregnancy: cook the chicken to 165 °F (74 °C).
Allergens: gluten (pearl couscous is wheat)
